To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rotation of the light atom around the heavy-heavy bond provides an important energy absorption mechanism for a triatomic molecule in an intense infrared laser field and the isomerization and the dissociation yields of a triatomic molecule can be greatly enhanced in the presence of a nonionizing picoseconds laser field.

(1) in the presence of a picosecond laser field, the rotational motion of the hydrogen atom around the CN bond provides an efficient mechanism for energy absorption, which is not accounted for when the system is restricted to two dimensions; (2) this energy absorption mechanism can generate considerable HCN--> HNC isomerization or high HCN rovibritional dissociation yield without preorientation of the system in the field; (3) this energy absorption and isomerization or dissociation mechanism is

the rotation of the hydrogen atom around the C=N bond plays an important role in the field driven isomerization and rovibrational dissociations of the HCN molecule, and that the isomerization and the dissociation of HCN in liquid Ar may be significantly suppressed by the presence of surrounding atoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the classical dynamics of a triatomic molecule HCN in a strong but non-ionizing infrared laser field.
the dynamics of HCN isomerization and rovibrational dissociations induced by strong picosecond infrared fields.
the dynamics of the isolated and the embedded HCN molecule in the picosecond infrared field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the full-dimensional classical dynamics of H-CN isomerization and rovibrational dissociations driven by an infrared picosecond laser field is significantly different from the dynamics obtained in a plane-wave field.
the field induced dynamics of the isolated HCN molecule is totally different from that of the HCN molecule in a liquid environment.

the full-dimensional classical dynamics is the most important and the most reliable theoretical approach to the study of the multiphoton rovibronic dynamics of polyatomic molecules in intense laser fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the full-dimensional classical dynamics of HNC-->HCN isomerization in the presence of an intense picosecond infrared field is very different from that found in the previous studies, which were based on the assumption that the H atom is fixed in the field direction.
the full-dimensional classical dynamics study of HCN in liquid Ar is a good model for the study of the full-dimensional quantum dynamics in liquid Ar.
the full-dimensional classical dynamics is a powerful tool for studying the dynamics of molecules in strong laser fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of a molecule driven by a laser field is strongly affected by all degrees of freedom of the molecule.
the full dimensionality of the problem must be considered in order to understand the dynamics of the system.

when all degrees-of-freedom are considered, a strong picosecond infrared field is capable of inducing isomerization and/or dissociation of triatomic molecules without preorienting or prealigning the molecule in the field.
